“Yesod fell. The world remembered old names. You answered.”

Oldenborn (Tideborne). Your place-soul is a shoreline that remembers every ship. You are the memory of tide-pools and drowned harbours, a genius loci clawing back into embodiment with salt still in the seams. Folk might call you a selkie or a drowned saint, because mortals label what scares them. You know the truth: you are a place-soul wearing legs.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Fey, Tideborne).
  • Size. Medium.
  • Speed. 6 squares.
  • Attributes. Oldenborn does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Soul in fiction and through Tier powers.

Oldenborn Core

At character creation you gain Old Memory, Old Flesh (Dream-Flesh, Old Paths, Veil-Sight, You Are Remembered) from the Oldenborn ancestry.

Tideborne Tier Powers

You gain Memory Tide at creation, then Undertow Grip at Initiation 5, Floodgate of Self at Initiation 11 and Ocean Judge at Initiation 17.

description.value:
“You are not an elf. You are the memory of a place that learned to walk again.”

Dream-Flesh. You do not sleep. When you rest, you drift into Yesod—symbolic memory-space—unless you choose otherwise. You are immune to magical sleep, and you can always tell when a dream, illusion, or constructed reality is present.

Old Memory, Old Paths. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret ruins, follow ley-lines, identify altered terrain, and sense metaphysical instability. You always know if a place feels remembered, abandoned, or contested (the GM answers vaguely).

Veil-Sight. You perceive the presence of spirits, ghosts, Spark echoes, and noospheric constructs. This grants awareness, not perfect sight.

You Are Remembered. When you first meet a community, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met with reverence, fear, or familiarity. It’s never neutral.

Depth-Sight. You can see normally in darkness and underwater (your eyes read pressure and motion).

Tide-sight. You have darkvision out to 12 squares.

"Every structure has a flaw. You only have to look at it correctly."

The Wyrdlens Adept turns perception into force. You run on Surge like everyone, and yours arrives when you land a manifestation (bank +1, max +2/round) — every revelation feeds the lens. The free Probability Overlay (1/round reroll-lowest, refreshes at the start of your turn) stays as your innate edge.

The Lens (spent via Surge)

  • Foresight (1) — you or an ally banks a reroll-lowest (you saw the thread).
  • Expose (2) — a foe's next attack and its saves are rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2 (you read the seam).
  • Refract (3) — an ally gains DR equal to Tier and a freed reaction (harm bends aside).
  • Revelation (5) — allies within 6 squares bank a reroll; a foe's next attack is rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.

Tikkun Sight endures — once per Soma Break, treat a misfire as a base-tier success (the Tree pays in Clarity instead).

Refraction: Anticipation — perception bent toward the next instant; routes, reactions, the moment before the moment.

The Refraction of Foresight reads time a half-second early. Your Surge spends are that edge made real: foreseen rerolls, an ally given room time shouldn't allow, and the strike that simply declines to land.

Refraction (spent via Surge)

  • Anticipation (1) — you and an ally each bank a reroll (foreseen).
  • The Slowed Instant (2) — an ally gains a freed reaction and DR equal to Tier.
  • The Stopped Strike (5) — a foe is Staggered and its next attack is rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.

Bound and Bargained

A sealed pact holds itself; you need only keep the terms.

Rules

While your Sealed Pact stance is active, the bindings carry part of your will for you: your Clarity maximum rises by 1.

Requires: Pactkeeper⚙ Applies automatically while the Sealed Pact stance is active: Clarity max +1.

You keep a quiet accounting of what should have gone wrong.

When you use a refraction die from Foresight Refraction to alter a roll and the result changes a failure into a success, mark one tally in your ledger.

  • At the end of the scene, if you have at least 2 tallies, you gain before a future scene (chosen by you) as the timeline pre-cooperates with your entry.
  • After you receive this initiative bonus once, your ledger resets to 0 tallies.

This is purely narrative bookkeeping: you’re getting credit for every disaster you quietly deflected.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Lens Ledger
Recovery: Tally-based  ·  Action: Free (passive bookkeeping)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
When a Foresight Refraction die converts a failure into a success, mark a tally. With 2+ tallies at scene end, gain an initiative bonus on a future scene of your choice; ledger then resets to 0.

Precognition through a repaired pane.

At the start of a scene (combat encounter, tense negotiation, or major exploration beat), roll 2d10 in secret and record the results as refraction dice.

  • Before any creature (including you) rolls a 2d10 for an attack, attribute check, or defense check, you may choose to replace that roll with one of your stored refraction dice.
  • You must decide before the 2d10 is rolled. Once used, a refraction die is expended.
  • You refresh your refraction dice at the start of each new qualifying scene.

Strategic Layer. Once per turn, you may spend 10 Intrigue marks to force an enemy faction to reroll one of its strategic 2d10-based checks (GM chooses the exact check if multiple candidates exist). You must accept the new result.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Foresight Refraction
Recovery: 2d10/scene + 1/turn  ·  Action: Free (declare before 2d10)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
At scene start, roll 2d10 in secret as refraction dice. Before any 2d10 (yours or anyone's) replace it with one stored die — declared before the roll. Strategic: 1/Turn, spend 10 Intrigue marks to force an enemy faction reroll.

Bladed Tempo

Your weapons are punctuation.

Rules

When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you may immediately draw or stow a weapon, or shift 1 square without provoking reaction strikes.

✍ Table rule.

You move in half-seen gaps between possible positions.

At the start of each of your turns, choose one creature you can see.

  • Until the start of your next turn, your movement does not provoke reaction strikes from that creature.
  • This effect ends early if you become Staggered or your movement is reduced to 0.

You don’t dodge them; you simply walk where their memory of you isn’t.

Adaptive Defense

Defense is not denial. It is management.

Rules

When you are hit by an attack you can see, you may use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your rank bonus + your Violence or Intrigue value (your choice).

🃏 Card — click ▶ when you are hit: it shows the reduction (rank bonus + Violence or Intrigue).

What steadies you can be refracted toward someone else.

When you succeed on a defense check, you can choose one ally within 6 squares who can see you.

  • That ally rerolls the lowest die on the next defense check they make within the next minute.
  • They must use the advantage before the end of that minute, or it is lost.

In fiction, this is you “sharing” a better path you just saw through danger.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Split Beam
Recovery: Trigger (defense success)  ·  Action: Free (after success)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
When you succeed on a defense check, an ally within 6 squares you can see reroll the lowest die on their next defense check within the next minute. Use it before the minute ends or it's lost.

activation.condition: When you succeed on a defense check.

description.value:
Occult Association (Bad Eden): Rosicrucian.

“I carry the old codes. I also carry a knife.”

Rosicrucians approach the Great Work like a courier network running through a burning city.

They preserve forbidden manuals, safeguard rituals, move people and knowledge between surviving nodes, and keep the chain of instruction alive when the world would prefer amnesia. Where some occult paths seek revelation or force, the Rosicrucian seeks continuity. The world cannot be repaired if the instructions are lost, the routes are severed, or the people who remember how to proceed are already dead.

To a Rosicrucian, the Great Work is not merely discovery. It is preservation, transit, and successful handoff.

How Rosicrucians pursue the Great Work:

  • By keeping archives, techniques, and living instruction intact
  • By building bridges between factions before they harden into wars
  • By turning safe passage into a strategic asset
  • By making recovered Sparks actually matter after recovery

Resonance: Netzach / Continuity — endurance, persistence, route-memory, and the stubborn Athletics of useful truth.

Tell-tales: precise manners, hidden caches, backup plans nested inside backup plans, and the calm confidence of someone who already mapped the exit.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 to your Domain's Diplomacy Domain rolls

Cost Principle: continuity creates obligation. Expect favors, route maintenance, political visibility, and pressure from everyone who now assumes your network will keep holding.

Domain edge: Your Domain earns +10 Diplomacy marks each turn while you serve it.
